title: Decouple rate-limit credit bucketization from account UTC offsets to prevent invoice skew
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Customers receiving rate-limit (burst) credits or late usage refunds are seeing incorrect invoice amounts when their account timezone offsets cause credit buckets to be assigned to adjacent invoice windows. The export/reconciler pipeline currently mixes UTC-anchored hour tiles with account-local billing windows in several places, producing duplicate or missing credit line items in NetSuite exports and Stripe invoice adjustments.

Root cause: The hourly aggregator that generates credit line candidates uses UTC-aligned 60-minute tiles (start-of-hour) for grouping, but the proration/assignment logic that picks which invoice to attach the credit to uses the account's billing anchor (billing_cycle_anchor) and an off-by-offset rounding step. When an account has a non-zero offset (e.g., +05:30) and a credit event occurs near the UTC boundary, the aggregator and assigner disagree about the tile boundary, causing credits to shift to the previous or next invoice. This manifests as: duplicate credits (credit generated in two adjacent windows), missing credits (credit falls outside the invoice export window and is held until next month), and proration drift on midcycle invoices.

Scope: Affects Hosted customers with non-UTC billing anchors and accounts with burst-rate-limit refunds or late usage adjustments between 2025-11-01 and 2026-02-28. Estimated ~1.2k invoices potentially affected, with a tail of smaller corrections.

Goals: 1) Make the bucketization deterministic and consistent across aggregation/export/reconciler stages by anchoring to a single canonical epoch per account (billing_cycle_anchor timestamp). 2) Ensure reconciler exports are idempotent (stable export_key) to avoid duplicates on retries. 3) Provide a safe backfill path to reconcile past affected invoices and generate minimal, auditable adjustments to Stripe/NetSuite.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregation and assignment use the same windowing function given an account billing anchor and timezone
Export rows include stable export_key composed of [account_id|billing_anchor|window_start|event_type]
End-to-end qa on staging reproduces the original bug with synthetic accounts and verifies fix eliminates duplicate/missing credits
Backfill tool can generate a reconciliation report and optionally emit Stripe adjustments or NetSuite credit memos for affected invoices
Monitoring detects regressions (new duplicate export_key occurrences) and alerts on >0.1% deviation for a production sample
implementation_notes: Introduce windowing utility: window_start = floor((event_ts - billing_anchor) / window_sec) * window_sec + billing_anchor
Use window_sec = 3600 for hourly tiles; make window_sec configurable per job; default to 3600
Update aggregator service (usage-aggregator) to compute and persist window_start and export_key at generation time
Update export/reconciler to read persisted window_start instead of recalculating using UTC-based logic
Add a unique constraint in export table on export_key to prevent duplicates (idempotency by DB uniqueness)
testing_plan: Unit tests for windowing util with a matrix of billing_anchor offsets (-12..+14), random event timestamps around boundaries
Integration tests: synthetic account in staging with billing_anchor +05:30 and events at UTC 23:58..00:02; assert single credit row emitted
End-to-end staging run: run reconciler, generate Stripe invoice preview, compare against golden snapshot
Load test: verify aggregator + reconciler throughput unchanged at production-scale (10k events/min) with windowing changes
Manual QA: finance review of produced NetSuite export CSV for a 30-day sample of impacted accounts
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gating: implement FEATURE_FLAG_DECUPLE_CREDIT_BUCKETING; default off
Deploy aggregator change to canary region with flag ON for 2% traffic for 48 hours
If stable, increase to 25% for 24 hours while observing duplicate-export-key metric
Flip flag to ON for all traffic and enable DB uniqueness constraint in a transactional migration
Run backfill job in dry-run mode to generate reconciliation report and required adjustments
Schedule finance approval window before emitting live Stripe/NetSuite adjustments; provide manual override per-account
backfill_strategy: Identify affected accounts by scanning export logs for duplicate/missing credit patterns between 2025-11-01 and 2026-02-28
For each account, recompute windowed credits using new windowing util and diff against already-exported lines
Classify diffs into: missing-credit, duplicate-credit, shifted-credit; produce an audit CSV with suggested Stripe credit or NetSuite credit memo
Expose a dry-run dashboard for finance to review suggested adjustments before posting
Rate-limit posting of adjustments to Stripe to 50 requests/min and NetSuite to 10 requests/min during backfill
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: export_key_conflicts.count (should trend to 0 after fix)
Alert: P1 if export_key_conflicts.rate > 0.05% over 5m and >10 events
Dashboard: sample of 500 accounts showing delta between aggregator window_start and reconciler-assigned_window
Audit log: link exported rows to Stripe invoice IDs and NetSuite memo IDs for finance reconciliation
dependencies: PM-412 (finance: backfill approval and posting window)
